, although in most cases the study of multiplex networks is not required for a correct understanding of the critical phenomena, in a few cases the multiplex structure can have an important effect and the study of the monoplex projection is not enough.

The main takeaway from our work is that
multiplex networks are more robust to random bond removal than their monoplex projections, but the extent to which this holds depends on how bonds are removed.
the multiplex network structure can be crucial for robustness, even in the case where the bond occupation probability is the same in all layers.
, in general, multiplex networks are more robust to random failure than their monoplex projections.
